name: ignite_search_sessions
description:
Search the public Ignite snapshot using English keywords/phrases or session codes.

    Keywords match any indexed term in the code, title, topics, speakers and the official
    description. Date is YYYY-MM-DD; time bounds are HH:MM in America/Los_Angeles. Empty
    keywords browse chronologically. Excludes unscheduled content by default. Returns at
    least 5 different sessions when possible: if keywords match fewer, sessions matching
    related_terms are added with match "related" (direct ones have match "keyword"). Returns
    instance IDs, facts, the official description, matched terms and lexical scores, NOT
    confidence. Use returned IDs with browser actions. No live seats or attendee data.

related_terms.title: Related Terms
related_terms.description: 3 to 6 broader or adjacent English words for the request (for "movie": video, media, streaming). Used only to fill the list up to 5 sessions when direct matches are fewer.

name: ignite_validate_agenda
description:
Review the calendar AFTER additions, or when the attendee asks for a review.

    Submit current agenda.instance_ids from the browser. Reports all time-overlap
    counts and venue-transfer gaps; detailed findings are bounded and explicitly
    marked if truncated. This never blocks adding, removes meetings, changes
    state, or connects to an external personal calendar. Walking times are not verified.

name: ignite_get_session
description: Get factual details and the full official description for one exact instance ID previously returned by search.

name: ignite_rank_sessions
description:
Rank the public Ignite snapshot by the attendee's interests and return a shortlist, best first.

    Give 1 to 8 short English interest phrases in priority order, 3 to 6 related_terms, plus
    optional Pacific date (YYYY-MM-DD), time window (HH:MM) and delivery filters. Titles, topics,
    speakers and official descriptions are searched. Each session code appears once. Always
    returns at least 5 sessions when anything is related: direct matches have match "strong";
    if there are fewer than 5, looser ones are added with match "partial" (shares a word) or
    "related" (matches a related term). Returns rank, exact instance IDs, a description excerpt,
    matched interests and a relative match_score (not a probability). Then call
    show_ranked_sessions with the IDs in the same order.

related_terms.title: Related Terms
related_terms.description: 3 to 6 broader or adjacent English words for the request (for "movie": video, media, streaming). Used only to fill the list up to 5 sessions when direct matches are fewer.
